title: Implement Forbidden Token and Mock Import Detectors
instructions: This chunk covers the FORBIDDEN_MODULES/FORBIDDEN_NAMES constants and AntiSpoofLinter.visit_Import/visit_ImportFrom. They serve the Code Forge audit gate (SRS-412-07-FR-002: 'The Code Forge DSP shall execute software development tasks governed by Scientific Summit peer-arbitration protocols') and the toolkit validation that validate_dsp_package runs on scaffolded plugins (SRS-412-07-FR-006, and NFR-DSP-01: 'New DSP plugins scaffolded via the toolkit shall compile and pass validation in less than 5 seconds'). The current code misses 'from unittest import mock', Mock/AsyncMock/NonCallableMock/create_autospec/patch imports, and 'import unittest.mock.x'. 'monkeypatch' in FORBIDDEN_NAMES never matches because it is a pytest fixture parameter, not an import name. Set FORBIDDEN_MODULES = {'unittest.mock', 'mock', 'pytest_mock'}. In visit_Import, flag any alias whose name is in FORBIDDEN_MODULES or starts with 'unittest.mock.' or 'mock.'. In visit_ImportFrom, flag node.module in FORBIDDEN_MODULES (or starting with 'unittest.mock.'), flag module 'unittest' importing alias 'mock', and flag any alias name in FORBIDDEN_NAMES = {'MagicMock', 'Mock', 'AsyncMock', 'NonCallableMock', 'create_autospec'}. Only flag 'patch' when it comes from a forbidden module, so unrelated 'patch' names are not false positives. Keep the existing message prefixes ('Forbidden mock import:', 'Forbidden mock from-import:', 'Forbidden mock name import:') and keep calling self.generic_visit(node). The four real packages src/cochem/dsp/{forge,press,pedagogy,toolkit} must still produce zero violations. Do not touch visit_Call or lint(). lint() never resets self.violations (lines 39-43, outside this chunk); report that separately rather than working around it here. Use no mock objects and no placeholder pass/NotImplError bodies. Existing tests do not cover the 'from unittest import mock' form; the listed tests guard against regressions and false positives.
